spec_match.rationale: Exercises the exact contract: a real fetch whose promise has resolved, then abort(reason) mid-body, inspecting what response.text() rejects with — the surface the ChromeStatus entry names.

interactive.rationale: One real streamed fetch per click against the site's slow-body route; every readout (timeline, verdict, observation table) is the browser's actual behavior.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index blurb promises the single-shot litmus with a marked custom reason; that is what the page runs.

edge_cases.rationale: Unreachable route and body-completed-before-abort races are both surfaced as labelled inconclusive outcomes, never as a verdict.

references.rationale: Links chromestatus.com/feature/5158507786665984, the Fetch Standard, and the sibling concepts.

conformance.rationale: The new feature suite's post-response-body-read-forwards-reason assertion runs the same litmus; it honestly fails on this pre-153 build and passes only when the reason is relayed.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 via CDP: litmus clicked, SUBSTITUTED verdict with generic AbortError observed and read back, console/network clean, desktop+mobile screenshots inspected.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts cover the ran and inconclusive branches with the observed name/forwarded flag in details.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables only; the forwarded verdict inverts to black-on-ivory with both colors set; result panel is charcoal on stone.

accessibility.rationale: Native button with 44px min height, role=status aria-live=polite readouts, observation table with scoped headers and aria-label.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: CDP matrix at 1280×800 and 360×740 DPR3: overflow 0 on both, no clipped controls, screenshots inspected. The harness run in this sandbox records broken solely because the runner cannot reach fonts.googleapis.com (ERR_CONNECTION_RESET) — an environment artifact, not a page defect.

openQuestions.title: Verify the FORWARDED verdict on Chrome 153+
openQuestions.detail: This runner is Chromium 141, so only the SUBSTITUTED branch could be observed live. On a Chrome 153+ (or Firefox) session, run the litmus and confirm the FORWARDED verdict renders with the marker message and same-object identity, and that the conformance assertions flip to pass.

guidanceConsulted.query: async action button pending state error retry accessible status live region
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Buttons driving async work need a disabled in-flight state and an accessible status region reflecting the outcome.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Run button disables during the litmus and re-enables in finally; verdict and log are role=status with aria-live=polite; no guidance doc covers abort-reason forwarding specifically, so general async-action guidance was applied.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: npx modern-web-guidance@latest search run 2026-08-09; closest ids custom-button-actions / full-session-analytics (AbortController usage).

summary: Verified with headless Chromium 141 via CDP: litmus produced the honest SUBSTITUTED verdict (generic AbortError, marker absent, identity false), inconclusive branches guarded, console/network clean, both viewport classes inspected.
